name: MN-07
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong R+18 district lean favors Fischbach
Markets price Fischbach at 97% to win
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: The R+18 district lean, Fischbach's incumbency and dominant fundraising advantage, and prediction markets pricing her at 97% all point to a safe Republican hold; Osberg's modest war chest gives no sign of a serious challenge.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Osberg within single digits, or a surge of outside spending against Fischbach, would be the first sign the race is closer than priced.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Michelle Fischbach seeks a third term in a western Minnesota district that leans Republican by about 18 points. She enters with a clear financial edge, having raised roughly $1.3 million and holding about $920,000 on hand, while Democrat Erik Osberg has raised about $330,000 with $114,000 available. No outside groups are meaningfully engaged on either side.

No public general-election polls cover the race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets give Fischbach about a 97% chance of winning. With the incumbent renominated and no evidence of a funded challenger surge, the seat is expected to remain comfortably in Republican hands.
